name: Mars 6
best_known_for: Soviet 1973 Mars lander — first descent telemetry from Mars atmosphere (224 s, mostly corrupted)
credit: Part of the Soviet four-spacecraft Mars wave of 1973 (Mars 4, 5, 6, 7) — and the only one to return useful science from a descent through Mars' atmosphere. Launched 1973-08-05 from Baikonur on a Proton-K, arrived 1974-03-12. The descent module separated from the flyby bus, entered the Martian atmosphere over Margaritifer Terra (23.90° S, 19.42° W), and returned 224 seconds of direct atmospheric telemetry — the first in-situ measurements of Mars' atmospheric temperature, pressure, and composition profile. However, due to a design flaw in the mass spectrometer's data system, a large amount of the data was corrupted and only partially recoverable. Signal was lost just before landing, during retrorocket firing; whether the lander crashed or survived to the surface is unknown. The flyby bus continued past Mars and acted as a relay station.
